# Test fixture licenses

Where each file under `tests/fixtures/` comes from and under which license it is committed
([PRD 34](../../docs/prd/34-testing.md) `PR-TST-016`, D-027). [`NOTICE`](../../NOTICE) names this
file for the vendored test fixtures instead of listing each paper itself. The same license is
declared for each file in [`REUSE.toml`](../../REUSE.toml), so `reuse lint` checks it
([licensing policy](../../docs/dev/licensing.md)). This file is a gated path: a change to it needs
the maintainer's approval (R-23).

## What may be committed here

- Synthetic text generated by [`scripts/gen_fixtures.py`](../../scripts/gen_fixtures.py) from a
  seed (`--list` prints the catalogue of fixture kinds, `--help` the options).
- A small set of open-access papers under CC-BY or CC0, vendored under `papers/`, each with a row
  below that names its source, DOI, license and attribution.
- Files that the test suites or the project's own dev scripts record: MCP contract transcripts,
  redacted resolver responses, storage databases.
- No other third-party text (D-027) and no unpublished data ([PRD 34 §4](../../docs/prd/34-testing.md#4-test-data-and-privacy)).
  The maintainer's own revision histories, exported with `tlilli export --canonical`, are used
  locally and at gates and are never committed.

## Fixture kinds

No fixture is committed yet: each directory arrives with the first test that uses it.

| Directory | Contents | Provenance | License |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `manuscripts/` | Synthetic manuscripts (Markdown) | Generated by `scripts/gen_fixtures.py`; the first line of each file names its seed | Apache-2.0, 2026 bioedca |
| `revisions/` | Revision corpora: scripted edit series over the synthetic manuscripts | Generated by `scripts/gen_fixtures.py` (generator pending, v0.1) | Apache-2.0, 2026 bioedca |
| `papers/` | Open-access papers | Vendored by hand; one row each under [Vendored papers](#vendored-papers) | CC-BY or CC0, per paper |
| `transcripts/` | Golden JSON-RPC transcripts | Recorded by the MCP contract tests ([PRD 34 §1](../../docs/prd/34-testing.md#1-test-layers)) | Apache-2.0, 2026 bioedca |
| `http/` | Resolver responses, redacted | Recorded by a dev script (`PR-TST-006`) | Per host, recorded in this file with the first response from that host |
| `db/` | One storage database per released schema version | Written by the release that introduces the schema ([ADR-0004](../../docs/adr/0004-storage-schema-v1-and-migrations.md)) | Apache-2.0, 2026 bioedca |

## Adding a paper

1. Check on the publisher's page that the paper is licensed CC-BY (any version) or CC0, and keep
   the page's URL. Any other license, CC-BY-NC, CC-BY-ND and "free to read" included, is refused.
2. Put the files under `papers/<first-author>-<year>-<short-title>/`, unchanged except as the
   Changes column says.
3. Add a row above: path, title, attribution as the license asks for it, DOI, source URL, SPDX
   identifier (`CC-BY-4.0`, `CC0-1.0`, ...), retrieval date and changes.
4. Add an `[[annotations]]` table for `tests/fixtures/papers/<slug>/**` at the end of `REUSE.toml`,
   with the copyright holder as the paper names it and the same SPDX identifier. The Apache-2.0
   table also matches `.md`, `.txt` and `.json` files, so `reuse lint` cannot tell when this table
   is missing for those kinds; review checks the row and the table together.
5. If `LICENSES/` lacks the license text, add it with `reuse download <SPDX-ID>` (`LICENSES/` is a
   gated path too). Then run `scripts/ci.sh reuse`.
